title.zh: 卷245 列傳三十二 刚林 冯铨 陈铭夏 陈之遴 刘正宗
title.en: Volume 245 Biographies 32: Gang Lin, Feng Quan, Chen Mingxia, Chen Zhilin, Liu Zhengzong
title.raw: 卷245 列傳三十二 刚林 冯铨 陈铭夏 陈之遴 刘正宗

sentences.zh: 剛林，瓜爾佳氏，字公茂，滿洲正黃旗人，世居蘇完。

translations.literal: Gang Lin, of the Guwalgiya clan, style name Gongmao, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner whose family had long resided in Suwan.
translations.idiomatic: Gang Lin, of the Guwalgiya clan, styled Gongmao, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner from a family that had long lived in Suwan.

sentences.zh: 初來歸，隸正藍旗，屬郡王阿達禮。

translations.literal: When he first came to submit, he was enrolled in the Bordered Blue Banner and placed under Prince Adali.
translations.idiomatic: When he first submitted, he was assigned to the Bordered Blue Banner and served under Prince Adali.

sentences.zh: 授筆帖式，掌繙譯漢文。

translations.literal: He was appointed a bithesi and put in charge of translating Chinese texts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a bithesi clerk and placed in charge of translating Chinese documents.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，以漢文應試，中式舉人，命直文館。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, he took the examination in Chinese, passed as a provincial graduate, and was ordered to serve in the Literary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiancong (1634), he sat for the Chinese examination, passed as a provincial graduate, and was assigned to the Literary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，授國史院大學士，與範文程、希福等參與政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the State History Academy and, with Fan Wencheng, Hifu, and others, took part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636), he was made Grand Secretary of the State History Academy and joined Fan Wencheng, Hifu, and others in managing government affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏請重定部院承政以下官各五等，又疏請定試士之法，皆報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reestablish five grades for all offices from the department directors and commissioners downward, and again memorialized to fix the method for examining scholars; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials to reclassify officials from department directors downward into five grades and to set rules for civil examinations; the court approved both.

sentences.zh: 太宗四征不庭，疆宇日闢。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor campaigned four times against those who would not come to court, and the realm expanded day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji led four campaigns against recalcitrant states, and the empire steadily expanded.

sentences.zh: 剛林屢奉使軍前，宣布威德，咸稱上旨。

translations.literal: Gang Lin was repeatedly sent on missions to the armies to proclaim imperial majesty and virtue, and all said it accorded with the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gang Lin was repeatedly dispatched to the front to proclaim the emperor's authority and benevolence, and all acknowledged that he spoke with the throne's intent.

sentences.zh: 積功，授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was granted the hereditary office of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he received the hereditary rank of niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 八年，阿達禮有罪，改隸正黃旗。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Adali was found guilty, and [Gang Lin] was transferred to the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Adali was condemned, Gang Lin was reassigned to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎，進世職二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor established the capital, [Gang Lin] was advanced to second-rank hereditary jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shunzhi Emperor fixed the capital at Beijing, Gang Lin was promoted to second-rank hereditary jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 三年、四年，迭主會試。

translations.literal: In the third and fourth years he presided over the metropolitan examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third and fourth years he served in turn as chief examiner of the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 考滿，進世職一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When his term review was completed, he was advanced to first-rank hereditary adaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: After a satisfactory performance review, he was promoted to first-rank hereditary adaha hafan.

sentences.zh: 五年，復進三等阿思哈尼哈番，賜號「巴克什」。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was further advanced to third-rank ashan i hafan and granted the title "Baksi."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was further raised to third-rank ashan i hafan and given the honorific title Baksi.

sentences.zh: 六年，充太宗實錄總裁，復主會試。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Taizong and again presided over the metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made chief compiler of Hong Taiji's Veritable Records and again chaired the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 疏請令六科錄諸臣章奏並批答，月送史館，備纂修國史，報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Six Offices of Scrutiny should record all ministers' memorials and imperial rescripts and send them monthly to the History Academy to prepare compilation of the national history; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that the Six Offices of Scrutiny copy every minister's memorial and the emperor's response each month to the History Academy for use in compiling the national history; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，以編撰明史闕天啟四年至七年實錄，請敕懸賞購求；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because the compilation of the History of Ming lacked the Veritable Records for the fourth through seventh years of Tianqi, he requested an edict offering rewards for their purchase;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, noting that work on the History of Ming lacked the Veritable Records for Tianqi years 4–7, he asked that an edict offer a bounty for their recovery;

sentences.zh: 崇禎一朝事責無考，其有野史、外傳，並令訪送。

translations.literal: matters of the Chongzhen reign had no responsible compiler and could not be verified, and any unofficial histories or outside accounts were also ordered to be sought and forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: and because Chongzhen-era affairs had no reliable record, any unofficial histories or outside accounts were likewise to be sought out and delivered.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate agencies.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞薨，得罪。

translations.literal: Prince Regent Dorgon died and was found guilty posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Regent Dorgon died, he was posthumously condemned.

sentences.zh: 剛林阿附睿親王，參與移永平密謀，又與大學士祁充格擅改太祖實錄，為睿親王削匿罪愆、增載功績，坐斬，籍沒。

translations.literal: Gang Lin had fawned on the Prince Regent, took part in the secret plot to move Yongping, and together with Grand Secretary Qi Chongge had altered the Veritable Records of Taizu without authorization, erasing Dorgon's offenses and inflating his merits; he was sentenced to decapitation and his property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Gang Lin had curried favor with Dorgon, joined the secret Yongping conspiracy, and with Grand Secretary Qi Chongge had tampered with Taizu's Veritable Records to conceal Dorgon's crimes and exaggerate his achievements; he was executed and his estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 祁充格，烏蘇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，世居瓦爾喀。

translations.literal: Qi Chongge, of the Usu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner whose family had long lived in Warka.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Chongge, of the Usu clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner from a family long settled in Warka.

sentences.zh: 國初從其族吉思哈等來歸。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he came to submit with his kinsman Jisiha and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early years he submitted with his kinsman Jisiha and others.

sentences.zh: 太宗時號「四貝勒」，以祁充格嫺習文史，令掌書記。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time [the princes] were called the "Four Beile"; because Qi Chongge was skilled in letters and history, he was ordered to manage secretarial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hong Taiji, known as the "Four Beile" period, Qi Chongge was put in charge of secretarial work because he was adept at literature and history.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，初設六部，授禮部啟心郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong, when the Six Ministries were first established, he was appointed Qixinlang of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiancong (1631), when the Six Ministries were first set up, he was made a Qixinlang in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，考績，授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, after a performance review, he was appointed niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after his performance review, he was appointed niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，睿親王多爾袞伐明，攻錦州，命鞏阿岱往濟師，祁充格從師有功，還報捷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, Prince Regent Dorgon campaigned against Ming and attacked Jinzhou; Gongadai was ordered to reinforce the army, and Qi Chongge followed the campaign with merit and returned to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636), Dorgon attacked Ming forces at Jinzhou; when Gongadai was sent to reinforce the army, Qi Chongge served with distinction and returned bearing news of victory.

sentences.zh: 三年，睿親王復伐明，太宗親餞於郊。

translations.literal: In the third year the Prince Regent again campaigned against Ming, and Taizong personally saw him off in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Dorgon again marched against Ming, and Hong Taiji personally saw him off outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 祁充格以不啟豫親王多鐸從上出送，又於是日私往屯莊，坐死，命寬之，奪官，貫耳鞭責，以隸睿親王。

translations.literal: Qi Chongge, for not informing Prince Dodo to accompany the emperor in seeing [Dorgon] off and for going privately to his estate that same day, was liable to death; he was ordered spared, stripped of office, given ear-piercing and flogging, and placed under the Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Chongge was condemned to death for failing to notify Prince Dodo to join the send-off and for visiting his private estate that day; the sentence was commuted to loss of office, ear-piercing, flogging, and reassignment to Dorgon's service.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，授弘文院大學士，充明史總裁官、冊封朝鮮世子正使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy, served as chief compiler of the History of Ming, and was chief envoy to invest the Korean crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2 (1645) he became Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy, chief compiler of the History of Ming, and chief envoy to invest Korea's crown prince.

sentences.zh: 四年，考滿，加授牛錄額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when his term review was completed, he was additionally granted niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after a satisfactory review, he was additionally granted the rank of niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 六年，充太宗實錄總裁官，與剛林等同主會試。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of Taizong's Veritable Records and, with Gang Lin and others, jointly presided over the metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was chief compiler of Hong Taiji's Veritable Records and, with Gang Lin and others, chaired the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 八年，與剛林同誅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was executed together with Gang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was executed alongside Gang Lin.

sentences.zh: 馮銓，字振鷺，順天涿州人。

translations.literal: Feng Quan, style name Zhenlu, was a native of Zhuozhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan, styled Zhenlu, came from Zhuozhou in Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Wanli reign, he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the Wanli era and was appointed a Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 諂事魏忠賢，累遷文淵閣大學士兼戶部尚書，加少保兼太子太保，以微忤罷去。

translations.literal: He fawned on Wei Zhongxian and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrently Minister of Revenue, with added titles Junior Guardian and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; for a slight offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: By currying favor with Wei Zhongxian he rose to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and Minister of Revenue, with the added titles Junior Guardian and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, until a minor clash of wills cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝既誅忠賢，得銓罷官後壽忠賢百韻詩，論杖徒，贖為民。

translations.literal: After the Chongzhen Emperor had executed Zhongxian, a hundred-rhyme birthday poem for Zhongxian that Feng Quan had written after his dismissal was discovered; he was sentenced to beating and penal servitude, then ransomed back to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongzhen executed Wei Zhongxian, officials found a hundred-rhyme birthday poem Feng had written for Zhongxian after his own dismissal; he was sentenced to beating and exile, then ransomed back to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，睿親王既定京師，以書徵銓，銓聞命即至，賚冠服、鞍馬、銀幣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, after the Prince Regent had secured the capital, he summoned Feng Quan by letter; Feng came as soon as he heard the order and was given caps and robes, saddle horses, and silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 1 (1644), after Dorgon secured Beijing, he summoned Feng Quan by letter; Feng came at once and was rewarded with court dress, horses, and silver.

sentences.zh: 令以大學士原銜入內院佐理機務，與大學士洪承疇疏請復明票擬舊制，又與大學士謝升等議定郊社、宗廟樂章。

translations.literal: He was ordered to enter the Inner Court in his former grand secretary rank to assist in state affairs; with Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou he memorialized to restore the Ming practice of drafting rescripts, and with Grand Secretary Xie Sheng and others he settled the music for suburban and ancestral rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to join the Inner Court at his former grand secretary rank to help manage affairs; with Hong Chengchou he petitioned to restore Ming-style draft rescripts, and with Xie Sheng and others he fixed the music for suburban and ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，世祖禦皇極門受賀，給事中孫承澤疏糾朝班雜亂，語侵內院。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month the Shizu Emperor took the imperial seat at the Huangji Gate to receive congratulations; Supervising Secretary Sun Chengze memorialized to correct disorder in the court ranks, with words that impugned the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month the Shunzhi Emperor received congratulations at the Huangji Gate; Supervising Secretary Sun Chengze complained of disorder in the court ranks in language that criticized the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 銓與升、承疇乞罷，諭令益殫忠猷，以襄新治。

translations.literal: Feng Quan, Xie Sheng, and Hong Chengchou begged to resign; they were instructed to devote their loyal counsel all the more to assist the new rule.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan, Xie Sheng, and Hong Chengchou asked to resign, but were told to redouble their loyal service in support of the new regime.

sentences.zh: 二年，授弘文院大學士兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy and concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 御史吳達劾銓向降將薑瓖索銀三萬，許以封拜，未稱其意；

translations.literal: Censor Wu Da impeached Feng Quan for demanding thirty thousand taels of silver from the surrendered general Jiang Xiang, promising enfeoffment, which did not satisfy [Jiang];
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Da accused Feng Quan of demanding thirty thousand taels from the surrendered general Jiang Xiang in exchange for a title, which failed to satisfy him;

sentences.zh: 內院政本所關，乃令其子源淮擅入，張宴歡飲。

translations.literal: the Inner Court being where the foundations of government lie, [Feng Quan] nevertheless had his son Yuanhuai enter without authorization and set out a feast with merry drinking.
translations.idiomatic: yet because the Inner Court was the heart of government, he still had his son Yuanhuai enter without leave and hold a lavish banquet.

sentences.zh: 給事中許作梅、莊憲祖、杜立德，御史王守履、羅國士、鄧孕槐、桑芸等亦交章劾銓得招撫侍郎江禹緒金；

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Xu Zuomei, Zhuang Xianzu, and Du Lide, and Censors Wang Shoulü, Luo Guoshi, Deng Yunhuai, Sang Yun, and others also submitted successive memorials impeaching Feng Quan for receiving gold from Pacification Vice Minister Jiang Yuxu;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Xu Zuomei, Zhuang Xianzu, and Du Lide, and Censors Wang Shoulü, Luo Guoshi, Deng Yunhuai, and Sang Yun also filed memorials accusing Feng of taking gold from Pacification Vice Minister Jiang Yuxu;

sentences.zh: 為源淮賄招撫侍郎孫之獬充標下中軍；

translations.literal: for bribing Pacification Vice Minister Sun Zhixi to appoint Yuanhuai as a company commander under his banner;
translations.idiomatic: and of bribing Pacification Vice Minister Sun Zhixi to make Yuanhuai a company commander in his command;

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎李若琳為銓黨羽，庸懦無行。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Li Ruolin was Feng Quan's partisan, mediocre, timid, and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Li Ruolin was Feng's ally—mediocre, timid, and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 御史李森先疏繼入，語尤峻，略謂：「明二百餘年國祚，壞於忠賢，而忠賢當日殺戮賢良，通賄謀逆，皆成於銓。

translations.literal: Censor Li Senxian followed with a memorial in especially harsh language, saying in summary: "The more than two hundred years of Ming fortune were ruined by Zhongxian, and Zhongxian's slaughter of the worthy, bribery, and plotting of rebellion were all brought about by Feng Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Senxian followed with an even harsher memorial, arguing in essence: "More than two centuries of Ming rule were ruined by Wei Zhongxian, and Zhongxian's slaughter of the worthy, bribery, and treason were all engineered by Feng Quan.

sentences.zh: 此通國共知者。

translations.literal: This is known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This is known to the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 請立彰大法，戮之於市。

translations.literal: I beg that the law be made manifest and that he be executed in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the law be upheld and that he be executed in public."

sentences.zh: 」疏並下刑部鞫問，刑部以所劾不實，啟睿親王。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent down to the Ministry of Justice for inquiry; the Ministry held the charges untrue and reported to the Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials were referred to the Ministry of Justice, which found the charges unsubstantiated and reported to Prince Regent Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 王集廷臣覆讞，以銓降後與之獬、若琳皆先薙發，之獬家男婦並改滿裝，諸臣遂謀陷害。

translations.literal: The Prince assembled the court ministers to reexamine the case and held that after Feng Quan's surrender he, Sun Zhixi, and Li Ruolin had all shaved their foreheads first; the men and women of Sun Zhixi's household had also adopted Manchu dress, and the ministers were therefore plotting to frame them.
translations.idiomatic: Dorgon convened the ministers to rehear the case and argued that Feng Quan, Sun Zhixi, and Li Ruolin had all shaved their foreheads after surrender, and that Sun's household had adopted Manchu dress—the accusers were trying to frame loyal collaborators.

sentences.zh: 王謂三人者皆恪遵本朝法度，詰責科道諸臣。

translations.literal: The Prince said all three had strictly observed the laws of the dynasty and rebuked the supervising secretaries and censors.
translations.idiomatic: Dorgon declared that all three had faithfully followed Qing law and rebuked the censorate officials.

sentences.zh: 給事中龔鼎孳言銓附忠賢作惡，銓亦反詰鼎孳嘗降李自成。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Gong Dingzi said Feng Quan had attached himself to Zhongxian in doing evil; Feng Quan in turn charged that Dingzi had once surrendered to Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gong Dingzi said Feng had aided Zhongxian's crimes; Feng retorted that Dingzi had once surrendered to Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 王問鼎孳：「銓語實否？

translations.literal: The Prince asked Dingzi: "Is Feng Quan's statement true?
translations.idiomatic: Dorgon asked Dingzi: "Is what Feng Quan says true?

sentences.zh: 」鼎孳曰：「豈惟鼎孳，魏徵亦嘗降唐太宗。

translations.literal: " Dingzi said: "Not only Dingzi—even Wei Zheng once surrendered to Emperor Taizong of Tang."
translations.idiomatic: " Dingzi replied: "Not only I—even Wei Zheng once submitted to Tang Taizong."

sentences.zh: 」王因斥鼎孳，遂寢其事。

translations.literal: The Prince thereupon rebuked Dingzi and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Dorgon rebuked Dingzi and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 以森先言過甚，奪官，互見森先傳。

translations.literal: Because Senxian's words had been excessive, his office was taken away; see also the biography of Senxian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Senxian was stripped of office for going too far; see his biography for the full account.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，銓疏言：「臣蒙特召入內院，列同官舊臣之前，臣固辭不敢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Feng Quan memorialized: "Your servant was specially summoned to the Inner Court and ranked before fellow officials who were old ministers; your servant firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Feng Quan wrote: "Your servant was specially summoned to the Inner Court and placed ahead of long-serving colleagues; I firmly declined, not daring to accept.

sentences.zh: 攝政王面諭：'國家尊賢敬客，卿其勿讓！

translations.literal: The Prince Regent instructed me in person: 'The state honors the worthy and respects guests—do not decline!'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent told me in person: 'The state honors talent and welcomes guests—you must not refuse!'

sentences.zh: '今海宇漸平，制度略定。

translations.literal: 'Now the realm is gradually pacified and institutions are largely settled.
translations.idiomatic: 'The realm is gradually pacified and institutions are largely in place.

sentences.zh: 金台駿骨，暫示招徠。

translations.literal: The golden terrace seeks fine steeds—this is only a temporary gesture of recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: The throne seeks able men—this is only a temporary gesture of recruitment.

sentences.zh: 久假不歸，實逾涯分。

translations.literal: To hold office long without returning [to proper bounds] truly exceeds one's proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: To remain in office so long without stepping back truly exceeds what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 況叨承寵命，賜婚滿洲，理當附籍滿洲編氓之末。

translations.literal: Moreover I have presumptuously received favor and been granted marriage into the Manchu [clan]; by rights I ought to be enrolled at the end of the Manchu registers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have received extraordinary favor, including marriage into a Manchu clan, and ought by rights to rank at the end of the Manchu registers.

sentences.zh: 回繹尊賢敬客之諭，輾轉悚懼，特懇改列範文程、剛林後。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the instruction to honor the worthy and respect guests, I am repeatedly fearful and beg especially to be placed after Fan Wencheng and Gang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the charge to honor talent, I am deeply uneasy and beg to be ranked after Fan Wencheng and Gang Lin.

sentences.zh: 如以新舊為次，並當列祁充格、寧完我後。

translations.literal: If seniority by old and new is the rule, I should also be placed after Qi Chongge and Ning Wanwo."
translations.idiomatic: If precedence follows seniority, I should also stand after Qi Chongge and Ning Wanwo."

sentences.zh: 」得旨：「天下一統，滿、漢無分別。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Under unified rule under Heaven, Manchu and Han are without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "Under unified rule, Manchu and Han are not to be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 內院職掌等級，原有成規，不必再定。

translations.literal: The duties and ranks of the Inner Court already have established rules and need not be fixed anew."
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Court already has established ranks; there is no need to redefine them."

sentences.zh: 」是年命典會試，列範文程、剛林後，寧完我前。

translations.literal: That year he was ordered to preside over the metropolitan examinations, ranked after Fan Wencheng and Gang Lin and before Ning Wanwo.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was ordered to chair the metropolitan examinations, placed after Fan Wencheng and Gang Lin but before Ning Wanwo.

sentences.zh: 四年，复典會試。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again presided over the metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again chaired the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 六年，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the added titles Junior Tutor and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Junior Tutor and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，上親覈諸大臣功績，諭：「銓先經吳達奏劾得叛將薑瓖賄，便當引去；

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor personally reviewed the merits of the grand ministers and instructed: "Feng Quan was earlier impeached by Wu Da for taking bribes from the rebel general Jiang Xiang and ought to have withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor personally reviewed the grand ministers' records and said: "When Wu Da accused Feng Quan of taking bribes from the rebel Jiang Xiang, Feng should have resigned;

sentences.zh: 乃隱忍居官，七年以來，無所建白：令致仕。

translations.literal: yet he concealed the matter and remained in office; for seven years he has offered nothing constructive: order him to retire."
translations.idiomatic: yet he stayed on; for seven years he has offered nothing of value—let him retire."

sentences.zh: 李若琳憸險專擅，與銓朋比為奸，奪官，永不敘用。

translations.literal: Li Ruolin is treacherous, dangerous, and domineering, and in league with Feng Quan in wickedness; strip him of office and never employ him again."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruolin is treacherous and domineering and has conspired with Feng Quan—strip him of office and never employ him again."

sentences.zh: 」銓既罷，代以陳名夏，坐事奪官；

translations.literal: After Feng Quan was dismissed, Chen Mingxia replaced him but lost office for an offense;
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Quan left office, Chen Mingxia replaced him but was soon dismissed for misconduct;

sentences.zh: 代以陳之遴，亦不久罷。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin replaced him and was also soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin replaced him and was dismissed not long after.

sentences.zh: 上復召銓還，諭曰：「國家用人，使功不如使過。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned Feng Quan back and instructed: "In employing men, the state uses those with faults rather than those with mere merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Feng Quan and said: "In appointing men, it is better to use those who have erred than those who merely claim merit.

sentences.zh: 銓素有才學，博洽諳練，朕特召用，以觀自新。

translations.literal: Feng Quan has long had talent and learning, is broadly versed and experienced; We specially summon him to see whether he will renew himself."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan has long been learned and experienced; I summon him specially to see whether he will reform."

sentences.zh: 」銓至，召見，又與承疇、文程等同夕對論翰林官賢否，上曰：「朕將親試之！

translations.literal: When Feng Quan arrived he was received in audience; that evening, together with Hong Chengchou and Fan Wencheng, they discussed which Hanlin officials were worthy, and the emperor said: "I shall test them in person!"
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Quan arrived he was received in audience; that evening he joined Hong Chengchou and Fan Wencheng in discussing which Hanlin officials were fit for office, and the emperor said: "I shall test them myself!"

sentences.zh: 」銓奏曰：「南人優於文而行不符，北人短於文而行或善。

translations.literal: Feng Quan submitted: "Southerners excel in letters but their conduct does not match; northerners are weak in letters but their conduct may be good.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan replied: "Southerners excel at writing but their conduct often falls short; northerners are weaker in letters but their conduct may be sound.

sentences.zh: 今取文行兼優者用之可也。

translations.literal: Now we should select those excellent in both letters and conduct for employment."
translations.idiomatic: We should appoint those who excel in both learning and conduct."

sentences.zh: 」上頷之，仍授弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent and again appointed him Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded and reappointed him Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 以議總兵任珍罪坐欺飾論絞，上命寬之。

translations.literal: For discussing the offense of Regional Commander Ren Zhen he was sentenced to strangulation for deceit and concealment; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in the case of Regional Commander Ren Zhen he was sentenced to strangulation for concealing the facts; the emperor commuted the sentence.

sentences.zh: 銓入謝，奏對失旨，諭誡之。

translations.literal: Feng Quan entered to give thanks; his replies missed the imperial intent and he was admonished.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan came to give thanks, but his replies displeased the emperor and he was admonished.

sentences.zh: 龔鼎孳為左都御史，复劾銓，上命指實。

translations.literal: Gong Dingzi became Left Censor-in-Chief and again impeached Feng Quan; the emperor ordered specific facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong Dingzi became Left Censor-in-Chief he again impeached Feng Quan; the emperor demanded concrete evidence.

sentences.zh: 鼎孳言銓罪過頗多，惟以密勿票擬，非如諸曹有實可指，上切責鼎孳。

translations.literal: Dingzi said Feng Quan had many faults, but because of his confidential drafting of rescripts there were no concrete charges as with other offices; the emperor sharply rebuked Dingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi said Feng had many faults, but because his work was confidential drafting there was nothing concrete to cite, unlike other offices; the emperor sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，居母喪，命入直如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, while in mourning for his mother, he was ordered to attend court duty as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, while mourning his mother, he was ordered to continue regular attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 尋加少師兼太子太師。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the added titles Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上以銓衰老，加太保致仕，仍令在左右備顧問，銓疏請回籍，許之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because Feng Quan was aged, he was made Grand Guardian and ordered to retire, yet still kept at hand for consultation; Feng memorialized to return to his native place and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor, finding Feng Quan elderly, made him Grand Guardian and let him retire while keeping him nearby for advice; Feng asked to return home and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改設內閣，命以原銜兼中和殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Grand Secretariat was reorganized as the Cabinet, and he was ordered to serve in his former rank as concurrently Grand Secretary of the Zhonghe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when the Grand Secretariat became the Cabinet, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Zhonghe Hall at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，卒，諡文敏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi he died and was given the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Kangxi (1672) and was posthumously titled Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 旋命削諡。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered stripped of the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title was soon revoked.

sentences.zh: 孫之獬，山東淄川人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhixi was a native of Zichuan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhixi came from Zichuan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明天啟進士，授檢討，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the Tianqi reign, he was appointed reviser and promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A Tianqi-era jinshi, he was made a reviser and later promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 以爭毀三朝要典入逆案，削籍。

translations.literal: For disputing the destruction of the Essentials of Three Reigns he was entered in the treason case and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: For opposing the destruction of the Essentials of Three Reigns he was listed among traitors and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，侍郎王鰲永招撫山東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Vice Minister Wang Aoyong pacified Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 1, Vice Minister Wang Aoyong was sent to pacify Shandong.

sentences.zh: 土寇攻淄川，之獬斥家財守城。

translations.literal: Bandits attacked Zichuan; Zhixi spent his family wealth to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked Zichuan, Zhixi spent his family fortune to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫方大猷上其事，召詣京師，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shandong Governor Fang Dayou reported the matter; [Sun] was summoned to the capital and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Governor Fang Dayou reported his service; Sun was summoned to Beijing and made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二年，師克九江，之獬奏請往任招撫，從之，加兵部尚書銜以行。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the army took Jiujiang, Zhixi memorialized to go and serve in pacification; this was approved and he was given the acting rank of Minister of War for the mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after the army captured Jiujiang, Zhixi asked to go as pacification commissioner; the court agreed and gave him the acting rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三年，召還。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 總兵金聲桓劾之獬擅加副將高進庫、劉一鵬總兵銜，市恩構釁；

translations.literal: Regional Commander Jin Shenghuan memorialized impeaching Sun Zhixi for arbitrarily granting the rank of regional commander to deputy generals Gao Jinku and Liu Yipeng, currying favor and stirring up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Jin Shenghuan impeached Sun Zhixi for having arbitrarily bestowed regional-commander titles on Deputy Generals Gao Jinku and Liu Yipeng, trading favors and deliberately provoking conflict.

sentences.zh: 之獬議撫諸將懷觀望，不力攻贛州。

translations.literal: Sun Zhixi argued that the policy of pacification had left the generals hesitant and unwilling to press the attack on Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhixi maintained that the conciliation policy had bred hesitation among the commanders and kept them from pressing the assault on Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 之獬疏辨，下兵部議，奪之獬官。

translations.literal: Sun Zhixi submitted a memorial in his own defense; the matter was referred to the Board of War for deliberation, and Sun Zhixi was stripped of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhixi filed a memorial in rebuttal; the case went to the Board of War, which recommended that his office be taken from him.

sentences.zh: 四年，土寇復攻淄川，之獬佐城守，城破，死之，諸孫從死者七人，下吏部議卹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, local bandits again attacked Zichuan; Sun Zhixi assisted in the defense of the city; when the city fell, he died; seven of his grandsons died with him; the matter was referred to the Board of Personnel for deliberation on posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, local rebels again besieged Zichuan. Sun Zhixi helped hold the city, and when it fell he was killed, along with seven of his grandsons. The case was sent to the Board of Personnel to determine mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 侍郎陳名夏、金之俊議復之獬官，予卹；

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Chen Mingxia and Jin Zhijun recommended restoring Sun Zhixi's office and granting condolence compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Chen Mingxia and Jin Zhijun argued that Sun Zhixi's rank should be restored and that he should receive posthumous compensation.

sentences.zh: 馬光輝及啟心郎寧古里議之獬已削籍，不當予卹。

translations.literal: Ma Guanghui and the Keshinlang Ningguli argued that Sun Zhixi had already been struck from the registers and ought not receive condolence compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guanghui and the Keshinlang Ningguli held that because Sun Zhixi had already been removed from the rolls, he was not entitled to mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 兩議上，命用光輝議。

translations.literal: Both recommendations were submitted, and the emperor ordered that Ma Guanghui's recommendation be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When both opinions reached the throne, the emperor ruled in favor of Ma Guanghui's view.

sentences.zh: 李若琳，山東新城人。

translations.literal: Li Ruolin was a native of Xincheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruolin came from Xincheng, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明天啟進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the Ming he passed the jinshi examination in the Tianqi reign and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he earned his jinshi degree in the Tianqi reign and was appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，起原官，累遷少詹事，兼國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was restored to his former office and was successively promoted to vice grand secretary of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently serving as chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he was recalled to his former post and rose in stages to Vice Grand Secretary of the Hanlin Academy, while also serving as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 詹事府裁，改翰林院侍讀學士，兼祭酒如故。

translations.literal: When the Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent was abolished, he was changed to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, still concurrently holding the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: After the Heir Apparent's Secretariat was abolished, he was made a Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and continued to hold the chancellorship as before.

sentences.zh: 二年，請更定孔子神牌，復元制曰大成至聖文宣王，下禮部議，定稱大成至聖先師。

translations.literal: In the second year he requested that Confucius's spirit tablet be revised, restoring the Yuan designation as Perfect Sage and Ultimate Exemplar, Literary Propagation King; the matter was referred to the Board of Rites, which fixed the title as Perfect Sage and Ultimate Exemplar, Supreme Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he petitioned to revise Confucius's spirit tablet, proposing a return to the Yuan title Perfect Sage and Ultimate Exemplar, Literary Propagation King. The Board of Rites deliberated and settled on the form Perfect Sage and Ultimate Exemplar, Supreme Teacher.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again, this time to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，進尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the additional title of grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he received the additional rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 既罷歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed and returned home, he died not long afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Once dismissed and sent home, he died before long.

sentences.zh: 陳名夏，字百史，江南溧陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia, courtesy name Baishi, was a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia, styled Baishi, came from Liyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官修撰，兼戶、兵二科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the Ming he passed the jinshi in the Chongzhen reign, served as compiler, and concurrently held the posts of chief supervising secretary in both the revenue and war sections.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he took his jinshi in the Chongzhen reign, served as a compiler, and at the same time held the posts of Chief Supervising Secretary in the Revenue and War sections.

sentences.zh: 降李自成。

translations.literal: He surrendered to Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 福王時，入從賊案。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he was implicated in the case of following the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was caught up in the prosecution of those who had followed the rebel regime.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，詣大名降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he went to Daming to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he went to Daming and surrendered to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 以保定巡撫王文奎薦，復原官。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Wang Wenkui, governor-general of Baoding, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Baoding Governor-General Wang Wenkui, he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 入謁睿親王，請正大位。

translations.literal: He entered to pay homage to Prince Regent Dorgon and requested that Dorgon assume the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On being received by Prince Regent Dorgon, he urged the prince to take the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「本朝自有家法，非爾所知也。

translations.literal: The prince said: Our dynasty has its own ancestral regulations; this is not for you to know.
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied, This dynasty has its own house law. That is not a matter for you to speak of.

sentences.zh: 」旋超擢吏部侍郎，兼翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was exceptionally promoted to vice minister of personnel and concurrently reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was then swiftly elevated to Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently made Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 師定江南，九卿科道議南京設官。

translations.literal: When the army pacified Jiangnan, the nine ministers and the censorate officials deliberated on establishing offices in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After the armies had pacified Jiangnan, the Nine Ministers and the censorial officials debated how offices should be set up in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 名夏言：「國家定鼎神京，居北制南。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia said: The state has established its capital in the divine capital and governs the south from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia argued, The dynasty has fixed its seat in the sacred capital and rules the south from the north.

sentences.zh: 不當如前朝稱都會，設官如諸行省。

translations.literal: It should not, as in the previous dynasty, be called a capital metropolis with offices set up like those in the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing should not be treated, as under the previous dynasty, as a full secondary capital with a provincial-style bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 」疏入稱旨。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it accorded with the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial pleased the emperor when it reached him.

sentences.zh: 三年，居父喪，命奪情任事，請終制，賜白金五百，暫假歸葬，仍給俸贍其孥在京者。

translations.literal: In the third year, while in mourning for his father, he was ordered to serve without leaving mourning obligations; he requested to complete the mourning period; he was granted five hundred taels of silver, temporarily granted leave to return for the burial, and his salary was still paid to support his family remaining in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while mourning his father, he was ordered to remain in office despite the mourning period. He asked to observe full mourning, was granted five hundred taels of silver and temporary leave to bury his father, and continued to receive salary to support the family he had left in the capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，初設六部漢尚書，授名夏吏部尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Han Chinese ministers were first appointed to the Six Ministries, Chen Mingxia was appointed minister of personnel and given the additional title of grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Han ministers were first placed at the head of the Six Ministries, Chen Mingxia was made Minister of Personnel and given the additional rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，授弘文院大學士，進少保，兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy, promoted to junior guardian, and concurrently remained grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy, was promoted to Junior Guardian, and retained his concurrent rank as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 名夏任吏部時，滿尚書譚泰阿睿親王，擅權，名夏附之亂政。

translations.literal: When Chen Mingxia served as minister of personnel, the Manchu minister Tan Tai fawned on Prince Regent Dorgon and usurped power; Chen Mingxia attached himself to Tan Tai and participated in misgovernment.
translations.idiomatic: While Chen Mingxia held the Ministry of Personnel, the Manchu minister Tan Tai curried favor with Prince Regent Dorgon, seized power for himself, and Chen Mingxia attached himself to Tan Tai in corrupting the government.

sentences.zh: 睿親王薨，是夏，御史張煊劾名夏結黨行私，銓選不公，下王大臣會鞫，譚泰袒名夏，坐煊誣奏，論死。

translations.literal: When Prince Regent Dorgon died, that summer Censor Zhang Huang memorialized accusing Chen Mingxia of forming factions for private gain and making unfair appointments; the case was referred to a tribunal of princes and grand ministers; Tan Tai shielded Chen Mingxia; Zhang Huang was convicted of false accusation and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Regent Dorgon died that summer, Censor Zhang Huang impeached Chen Mingxia for factionalism, private dealing, and biased appointments. The case was sent to a joint tribunal of princes and senior ministers. Tan Tai protected Chen Mingxia, Zhang Huang was found guilty of false accusation, and he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 語詳煊傳。

translations.literal: The details are given in Zhang Huang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Zhang Huang's biography.

sentences.zh: 是時御史盛復選亦以劾名夏坐黜。

translations.literal: At that time Censor Sheng Fuxuan was also dismissed for impeaching Chen Mingxia.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time, Censor Sheng Fuxuan was punished with dismissal for having impeached Chen Mingxia.

sentences.zh: 迨秋，譚泰以罪誅，九年春，復命王大臣按煊所劾名夏罪狀，名夏辨甚力。

translations.literal: By autumn Tan Tai had been executed for his crimes; in the spring of the ninth year the emperor again ordered princes and grand ministers to investigate the charges Zhang Huang had brought against Chen Mingxia; Chen Mingxia defended himself vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Tan Tai was executed for his crimes. In the spring of the ninth year the emperor ordered princes and senior ministers to reopen the charges Zhang Huang had brought against Chen Mingxia, and Chen Mingxia defended himself with great force.

sentences.zh: 及屢見詰難，詞窮，泣訴投誠有功，冀貸死。

translations.literal: After repeated questioning, his words were exhausted; weeping, he pleaded that his surrender had merit and hoped to be spared from death.
translations.idiomatic: Under repeated interrogation he ran out of answers, wept, and pleaded that his early submission had been a service to the dynasty, hoping thereby to escape death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此輾轉矯詐之小人也，罪實難逭！

translations.literal: The emperor said: This is a slippery, deceitful petty man; his guilt truly cannot be evaded!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, This is a shifty, deceitful little man, and his guilt is real and hard to excuse!

sentences.zh: 但朕已有旨，凡與譚泰事干連者，皆赦勿問。

translations.literal: But I have already issued an edict that all those implicated in Tan Tai's affairs shall be pardoned and not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: But I have already decreed that everyone connected with Tan Tai's case is to be pardoned and left unprosecuted.

sentences.zh: 若復罪名夏，是為不信。

translations.literal: If I were again to convict Chen Mingxia, that would be breaking faith.
translations.idiomatic: If I now convict Chen Mingxia again, I would be breaking my word.

sentences.zh: 」因宥之，命奪官，仍給俸，發正黃旗，與閒散官隨朝，諭令自新。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was pardoned; he was stripped of office but still given salary, assigned to the Plain Yellow Banner to attend court with idle officials, and instructed to reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore spared, though stripped of office; he continued to draw salary, was assigned to the Plain Yellow Banner to attend court as an idle official, and was told to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 十年，復授秘書院大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again appointed grand secretary of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again made Grand Secretary of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書員缺，侍郎孫承澤請以名夏兼攝，上責承澤以侍郎舉大學士，非體。

translations.literal: When the post of minister of personnel fell vacant, Vice Minister Sun Chengyze requested that Chen Mingxia concurrently act in the role; the emperor rebuked Chengyze for recommending a grand secretary from the rank of vice minister, which was improper.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel fell vacant, Vice Minister Sun Chengyze proposed that Chen Mingxia serve concurrently as acting minister. The emperor rebuked Chengyze for having a vice minister recommend a grand secretary for the post, saying that this was improper.

sentences.zh: 翌日，命名夏署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The next day Chen Mingxia was ordered to serve as acting minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following day Chen Mingxia was ordered to serve as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上時幸內院，恆諭諸臣：「滿、漢一體，毋互結黨與。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited the Inner Court and constantly admonished the ministers: Manchus and Han are one body; do not form factions against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor visited the Inner Court he repeatedly warned his ministers, Manchus and Han are one body; do not band together in rival factions.

sentences.zh: 」名夏或強辭以對，上戒之曰：「爾勿怙過，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia sometimes answered with strong arguments; the emperor warned him: Do not rely on your faults and bring calamity upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia would sometimes answer back sharply, and the emperor cautioned him, Do not cling to your errors and bring ruin on yourself.

sentences.zh: 」諸大臣議總兵任珍罪，皆以珍擅殺，其孥怨望，宜傅重比。

translations.literal: The grand ministers deliberating on the crime of Regional Commander Ren Zhen all agreed that Ren had killed without authorization, that his family harbored resentment, and that a heavier penalty should be applied by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: In deliberating the case of Regional Commander Ren Zhen, the senior ministers agreed that Ren had killed without authorization, that his family nursed grievances, and that the penalty should be increased accordingly.

sentences.zh: 名夏與陳之遴、金之俊等異議，坐欺矇，論死，复寬之，但鐫秩俸，任事如故。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia, along with Chen Zhilin, Jin Zhijun, and others, held a dissenting view; they were convicted of deceiving the throne, sentenced to death, but again pardoned—only their rank and salary were reduced, and they continued in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia, Chen Zhilin, Jin Zhijun, and others dissented. They were found guilty of deceiving the throne and sentenced to death, but were pardoned again; only their rank and salary were reduced, and they remained in office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士寧完我劾之，略言：「名夏屢蒙赦宥，尚复包藏禍心。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Grand Secretary Ning Wanwo memorialized against him, stating in summary: Chen Mingxia has repeatedly received pardons, yet still conceals treacherous intent in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Grand Secretary Ning Wanwo impeached him, writing in part, Though repeatedly spared, Chen Mingxia still harbors treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂臣曰：'留發复衣冠，天下即太平。

translations.literal: He once told me: If hair were kept and robes and caps restored, all under heaven would at once be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He once told me, If we kept our hair and restored Ming dress, the realm would be at peace at once.

sentences.zh: '其情叵測。

translations.literal: His intentions cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: His true intentions are impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 名夏子掖臣，居鄉暴惡，士民怨恨。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia's son Yechen lived in the countryside committing violence and wickedness, arousing resentment among scholars and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia's son Yechen terrorized the countryside, and both gentry and common people hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 移居江寧，佔入官園宅，關通納賄，名夏明知故縱。

translations.literal: After moving to Jiangning, he seized government gardens and residences, used connections to accept bribes, and Chen Mingxia knowingly tolerated it.
translations.idiomatic: After moving to Jiangning he seized government gardens and mansions, used his connections to take bribes, and Chen Mingxia knowingly let him do it.

sentences.zh: 名夏署吏部尚書，破格擢其私交趙延先，給事中郭一鶚疏及之，名夏欲加罪，以劉正宗不平而止。

translations.literal: When Chen Mingxia was acting minister of personnel, he promoted beyond precedent his intimate associate Zhao Yanxian; Supervising Secretary Guo Yie memorialized about this; Chen Mingxia wished to punish him but stopped because Liu Zhengzong objected.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as acting Minister of Personnel, Chen Mingxia broke precedent to promote his crony Zhao Yanxian. Supervising Secretary Guo Yie memorialized against it. Chen Mingxia tried to punish Guo, but desisted when Liu Zhengzong protested.

sentences.zh: 浙江道員史儒綱為名夏姻家，坐事奪官逮問，名夏必欲為之复官。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang circuit official Shi Rugang was related to Chen Mingxia by marriage; when he was stripped of office and arrested for investigation, Chen Mingxia insisted on restoring his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang circuit intendant Shi Rugang was Chen Mingxia's in-law. When Shi was dismissed and arrested for investigation, Chen Mingxia pressed hard to have him restored to office.

sentences.zh: 給事中魏象樞與名夏姻家，有連坐事，應左遷，僅票俸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangshu was also related to Chen Mingxia by marriage; in a case of joint liability he should have been demoted, but only had his salary reduced on the roster.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangshu, another of Chen Mingxia's in-laws, was implicated in a joint-liability case and should have been demoted, yet received only a salary reduction on the roster.

sentences.zh: 護黨市恩，於此可見。

translations.literal: Protecting his faction and trading favors—this is evident from these cases.
translations.idiomatic: His protection of his clique and traffic in favors are plain from these examples.

sentences.zh: 臣等職掌票擬，一字輕重，關係公私；

translations.literal: We are charged with drafting memorials for imperial approval; the weight of a single character bears on public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: We are responsible for drafting memorials for imperial approval, and the weight of a single word can affect public and private interests alike.

sentences.zh: 立簿注姓，以防推諉。

translations.literal: We keep a register noting authors' names to prevent shifting blame.
translations.idiomatic: We keep a ledger recording each man's name so that responsibility cannot be evaded.

sentences.zh: 名夏私自塗抹一百十四字。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia privately altered one hundred and fourteen characters.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia privately erased or changed one hundred and fourteen characters.

sentences.zh: 上命誥誡科道官結黨，名夏擅加抹改，其欺罔類是。

translations.literal: The emperor had ordered a stern admonition against factionalism among censorate officials; Chen Mingxia's unauthorized alterations were deceit of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just issued a stern warning against factionalism among censorial officials, and Chen Mingxia's unauthorized alterations were deception of the same kind.

sentences.zh: 請敕大臣鞫實，法斷施行。

translations.literal: We request that grand ministers be commanded to investigate the facts and apply the law.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that senior ministers be ordered to establish the facts and punish him according to law.

sentences.zh: 」疏下廷臣會鞫，名夏辨諸款皆虛，惟「留發复衣冠」，實有其語。

translations.literal: When the memorial was referred for joint investigation by court officials, Chen Mingxia argued that all charges were false except keeping hair and restoring dress, which he had indeed spoken.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was sent for joint investigation, Chen Mingxia denied every charge as false except the remark about keeping hair and restoring Ming dress, which he admitted he had made.

sentences.zh: 完我與正宗共證名夏諸罪狀皆實，讞成，論斬，上命改絞。

translations.literal: Ning Wanwo and Liu Zhengzong jointly testified that all of Chen Mingxia's crimes were true; the verdict was completed and death by decapitation was recommended; the emperor ordered it changed to death by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Wanwo and Liu Zhengzong jointly confirmed that all the charges against Chen Mingxia were true. The verdict was finalized as decapitation, but the emperor ordered the sentence changed to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 掖臣逮治，杖戍。

translations.literal: Yechen was arrested, flogged, and exiled to military service.
translations.idiomatic: Yechen was arrested, beaten with the rod, and banished to frontier military service.

sentences.zh: 陳之遴，字彥升，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin, courtesy name Yansheng, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin, styled Yansheng, came from Haining, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，自編修遷中允。

translations.literal: In the Ming he passed the jinshi in the Chongzhen reign; he rose from compiler to court gentleman for fostering integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he earned his jinshi in the Chongzhen reign and rose from compiler to Court Gentleman for Fostering Integrity.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，來降，授秘書院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he came to surrender and was appointed reader-in-waiting of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he surrendered and was appointed Reader-in-Waiting of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was moved to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，加右都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the additional title of censor-in-chief of the right.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he received the additional rank of Censor-in-Chief of the Right.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 御史張煊劾大學士陳名夏，語涉之遴，鞫不實，免議，加太子太保，九年，授弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Huang impeached Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia; the language also implicated Chen Zhilin; the investigation found it unsubstantiated and he was exempted from prosecution; he was given the additional title of grand guardian of the heir apparent; in the ninth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Zhang Huang impeached Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia, the memorial also touched on Chen Zhilin, but the investigation found no substance to the accusation and he was cleared. He was given the additional rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and in the ninth year he became Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 時捕治京師巨猾李應試，王大臣會鞫，之遴默不語，王大臣詰之，之遴曰：「上立置應試於法則已，如或免死，則必受其害，是以不言。

translations.literal: At that time the great rogue of the capital Li Yingshi was arrested and prosecuted; when princes and grand ministers jointly examined the case, Chen Zhilin remained silent; when questioned, Chen Zhilin said: If Your Majesty immediately puts Yingshi to the law, that is enough; but if he were spared from death, he would surely cause me harm—therefore I do not speak.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the authorities were pursuing Li Yingshi, a notorious criminal of the capital. When princes and senior ministers jointly examined the case, Chen Zhilin said nothing. Pressed for an answer, he said, If Your Majesty puts Yingshi to death at once, that is enough. But if he is spared, he will surely turn on me. That is why I will not speak.

sentences.zh: 」王大臣等以聞，上以詰之遴，疏引罪。

translations.literal: The princes and grand ministers reported this; the emperor questioned Chen Zhilin; he submitted a memorial accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers reported this to the throne. The emperor questioned Chen Zhilin, and he submitted a memorial confessing his fault.

sentences.zh: 上以之遴既悔過，宥之。

translations.literal: Since Chen Zhilin had repented, the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chen Zhilin had shown repentance, the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 議總兵任珍罪，與名夏及金之俊持異議，坐罪，寬貸如名夏。

translations.literal: In deliberating on Regional Commander Ren Zhen's crime, he held a dissenting view with Chen Mingxia and Jin Zhijun; he was convicted but pardoned as Chen Mingxia had been.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated Regional Commander Ren Zhen's case, he sided with Chen Mingxia and Jin Zhijun against the majority. He was found guilty but pardoned in the same way Chen Mingxia had been.

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏請依律定滿臣有罪籍沒家產、降革世職之例，下所司議行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized requesting that the statutory precedents be applied for Manchu officials convicted of crimes—confiscation of family property and demotion or removal of hereditary offices—referring it to the appropriate offices for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized that Manchu officials convicted of crimes should be handled according to law, with confiscation of family property and reduction or removal of hereditary rank, and asked the relevant offices to deliberate and carry this out.

sentences.zh: 復授弘文院大學士，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He was again appointed grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy, given junior guardian and concurrently grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy and given the ranks of Junior Guardian and concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上幸南苑，召諸大臣入對，諭之遴曰：「朕不念爾前罪，屢申誥誡，嘗以朕言告人乎？

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor visited the Southern Park and summoned the grand ministers for audience; he said to Chen Zhilin: I have not held your past crimes against you and have repeatedly admonished you—have you ever told others what I said?
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to the Southern Park and summoned the senior ministers. He said to Chen Zhilin, I have overlooked your past offenses and warned you again and again. Have you ever repeated my words to others?

sentences.zh: 抑自思所行亦曾少改乎？

translations.literal: Or upon reflection, have you changed your conduct even slightly?
translations.idiomatic: Or, looking at your own behavior, have you changed even a little?

sentences.zh: 」之遴奏曰：「上教臣，臣安敢不改？

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin replied: Your Majesty has instructed me—how would I dare not reform?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin answered, Your Majesty has taught me—how could I dare not reform?

sentences.zh: 特臣才疏學淺，不能仰報上恩。

translations.literal: Only I am talent-poor and learning-shallow, unable to repay Your Majesty's grace from below.
translations.idiomatic: Only my talent is limited and my learning shallow, and I cannot adequately repay Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕非不知之遴等朋黨而用之，但欲資其才，故任以職。

translations.literal: The emperor said: It is not that I do not know Chen Zhilin and his ilk form factions—I use them because I wish to employ their talents, and therefore assign them to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, It is not that I do not know Chen Zhilin and men like him form factions. I employ them because I want to use their abilities, and so I give them office.

sentences.zh: 且時時教飭之者，亦冀其改過效忠耳。

translations.literal: And the constant teaching and discipline are also in hope that they will reform their faults and serve loyally.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I keep instructing and correcting them is that I still hope they will reform and serve loyally.

sentences.zh: 」因責左副都御史魏裔介等媕阿緘默，裔介退，具疏劾之遴植黨營私，當上詰問，但云「才疏學淺」，良心已昧；

translations.literal: Thereupon he rebuked Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and others for equivocal silence; Yijie withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial impeaching Chen Zhilin for cultivating factions and pursuing private interests—when the emperor questioned him, he only said talent-poor and learning-shallow, his conscience already clouded.
translations.idiomatic: He then rebuked Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and others for their timid silence. Afterward Yijie submitted a detailed impeachment accusing Chen Zhilin of building a faction and pursuing private interests. When the emperor had questioned him, Chen Zhilin had answered only that he was talent-poor and learning-shallow—a sign that his conscience was already dead.

sentences.zh: 並言之遴諷禮部尚書胡世安舉知府沈令式，旋為總督李輝祖所劾，是為結黨之據。

translations.literal: It also stated that Chen Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon impeached by Governor-General Li Huizu—this was proof of factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial also said that Chen Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon impeached by Governor-General Li Huizu, and that this showed collusion among allies.

sentences.zh: 給事中王楨又劾之遴市權豪縱，昨蒙詰責，不思閉門省罪，即於次日遨遊靈佑宮，逍遙恣肆，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Zhen also impeached Chen Zhilin for trading in power and acting arrogantly and recklessly; having been rebuked yesterday, he did not think to stay home and reflect on his guilt, but the very next day wandered freely at Lingyou Palace in unrestrained leisure—his crime brooked no punishment less than death.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Zhen also impeached Chen Zhilin for selling influence and behaving with arrogant license. Though rebuked only the day before, he did not stay home to reflect on his guilt but went the next day to stroll at Lingyou Palace in open dissipation—a crime, Wang argued, that deserved death.

sentences.zh: 之遴疏引罪，有云：「南北各親其親，各友其友。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin submitted a memorial accepting guilt, saying: North and south each honor their own kin and each befriend their own friends.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin submitted a confession in which he wrote, North and south each favor their own kin and each stand by their own friends.

sentences.zh: 」上益不懌，下吏部嚴議，命以原官發盛京居住。

translations.literal: The emperor grew even more displeased; the matter was referred to the Board of Personnel for severe deliberation; he was ordered to remain in his original office but sent to live in Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still angrier. The case went to the Board of Personnel for severe deliberation, and Chen Zhilin was ordered to keep his former rank while being sent to live in Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 是冬，復命回京入旗。

translations.literal: That winter he was again ordered to return to the capital and enter a banner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was ordered back to the capital and enrolled in a banner.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復坐賄結內監吳良輔，鞫實，論斬，命奪官，籍其家，流徙尚陽堡，死徙所。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was again convicted of bribing and colluding with eunuch Wu Liangfu; the facts were established; death by decapitation was recommended; he was stripped of office, his property confiscated, and he was exiled to Shangyang Fort, where he died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was again found guilty of bribing and colluding with the eunuch Wu Liangfu. The facts were proved, decapitation was recommended, and he was stripped of office, his property confiscated, and exiled to Shangyang Fort, where he died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 劉正宗，字可宗，山東安丘人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong, courtesy name Kezong, was a native of Anqiu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong, styled Kezong, came from Anqiu, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，自推官授編修。

translations.literal: In the Ming he passed the jinshi in the Chongzhen reign; from magistrate's assistant he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he earned his jinshi in the Chongzhen reign and rose from magistrate's assistant to compiler.

sentences.zh: 福王時，授中允。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he was appointed court gentleman for fostering integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was made Court Gentleman for Fostering Integrity.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，以薦起國史院編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, on recommendation he was appointed compiler at the State History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he was recommended and appointed a compiler in the State History Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to academician of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Academician of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授吏部侍郎，擢弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed vice minister of personnel and promoted to grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書缺員，諭以「正宗清正耿介，堪勝此任，加太子太保，管吏部尚書」。

translations.literal: When the post of minister of personnel fell vacant, an edict stated: Zhengzong is upright and incorruptible, fit for this duty; grant him grand guardian of the heir apparent and charge him with managing the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel fell vacant, an edict declared, Liu Zhengzong is upright and incorruptible and is fit for this post. Grant him the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and put him in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 御史楊義論部推越次，正宗與辨，執相詬詈。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Yi argued that the ministry's recommended promotions skipped proper order; Liu Zhengzong disputed this, and they reviled each other face to face.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Yang Yi charged that the ministry's slate of promotions had leapfrogged proper seniority, Liu Zhengzong argued back—and the two ministers exchanged heated abuse in person.

sentences.zh: 給事中周曾發，御史姜圖南、祖建明交章劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhou Zengfa, and Censors Jiang Tunan and Zu Jianming, submitted memorials in succession impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhou Zengfa, together with Censors Jiang Tunan and Zu Jianming, then filed memorial after memorial calling for his removal.

sentences.zh: 御史張嘉復以正宗昏庸衰老，背公徇私，疏請罷斥。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Jiafu, on the grounds that Liu Zhengzong was senile, incompetent, and betrayed the public for private gain, memorialized requesting his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Jiafu memorialized the throne to dismiss Liu Zhengzong, accusing him of feeble-minded old age, betrayal of public duty, and rank favoritism.

sentences.zh: 下部議，以無實據，寢其事。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation; for lack of substantiating evidence, it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent down for departmental review, but with no hard evidence to support the charges, it was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 給事中硃徽复劾正宗擅擬僉事許宸遷通政司參議，不由會推，又未專疏題明。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhu Hui again impeached Liu Zhengzong for on his own authority drafting the transfer of Vice Director Xu Chen to Vice Commissioner of the Communications Office, without joint recommendation and without submitting a separate explanatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhu Hui impeached Liu Zhengzong again, this time for drafting on his own authority the promotion of Vice Director Xu Chen to Vice Commissioner of the Communications Office—bypassing joint recommendation and failing even to submit a separate memorial explaining the move.

sentences.zh: 正宗以疏忽引咎，當俸，援恩詔以免。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong accepted blame for negligence, was assessed a salary fine, and invoked an amnesty edict to be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong took responsibility for negligence and was fined a portion of his salary, but invoked an amnesty edict to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 旋引疾乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Soon after he cited illness and requested retirement; it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: He soon after pleaded illness and asked to retire; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 辭尚書，命以兼銜回內院，加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He resigned his ministry post; he was ordered to return to the inner court with concurrent titles, promoted to Junior Guardian and concurrent Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned as minister and was ordered back to the inner court with concurrent honors, receiving the titles Junior Guardian and concurrent Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十四年，考滿，進少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, upon completion of his term evaluation, he was promoted to Junior Mentor and concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when his performance review came due, he was promoted to Junior Mentor and concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was transferred to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was reassigned as Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上以正宗器量狹隘，終日務詩文，廷議輒以己意為是，降旨嚴飭，並諭曰：「朕委任大臣，期始終相成，以愜簡拔初念。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because Liu Zhengzong was narrow-minded, spent all his days on poetry and prose, and always insisted his own views were correct in court deliberations, the emperor issued a stern admonition, also instructing: I entrust my ministers expecting mutual completion from start to finish, to satisfy my original intent in selecting them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor, finding Liu Zhengzong petty in spirit, consumed all day with poetry and belles-lettres, and stubbornly treating his own opinion as law in court debate, sent down a stern rebuke. He also commanded: When I place my trust in a minister, I expect us to see the work through together—to honor the reason I chose him in the first place.

sentences.zh: 故不忍加罪，時加申戒。

translations.literal: Therefore I am unwilling to punish; I only warn you from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have not yet punished you, but only warn you again and again.

sentences.zh: 當痛改前非，稱朕優容寬恕之意。

translations.literal: You ought to deeply reform past faults and live up to my lenient and forgiving intent.
translations.idiomatic: You must thoroughly mend your old ways and prove yourself worthy of my forbearance.

sentences.zh: 」十七年，自陳乞罷，不允。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal; it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he memorialized asking to be removed from office; again the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 左都御史魏裔介劾「正宗自陳奏內不敘上諭切責，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie impeached: In his memorial of self-statement Liu Zhengzong did not recount the emperor's stern rebuke—lack of a minister's propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie impeached him, writing: In his own memorial Liu Zhengzong never mentioned the emperor's sharp rebuke—a failure of the most basic ministerial decorum.

sentences.zh: 李昌祚叛案有名，票擬內升。

translations.literal: In the Li Changzuo rebellion case he was named, yet in the draft memorial he promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changzuo was implicated in a treason case, yet Liu Zhengzong's draft memorial nevertheless recommended his advancement.

sentences.zh: 先後薦董國祥、梁羽明，今皆事敗，被劾不自檢舉。

translations.literal: He successively recommended Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming; now both have had their affairs exposed in scandal; impeached yet he did not report on himself.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming in turn; both have since been ruined by scandal, yet when impeached he did not confess his own part.

sentences.zh: 欺君之罪何辭？

translations.literal: What excuse is there for the crime of deceiving the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: What defense can there be for deceiving the throne?

sentences.zh: 正宗與張縉彥為友，縉彥序正宗詩曰'將明之才'，詭譎尤不可解。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong was friends with Zhang Jinyan; Zhang Jinyan's preface to Liu Zhengzong's poetry says talent for bringing clarity—especially baffling in its deviousness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong counted Zhang Jinyan among his friends; Zhang Jinyan's preface to Liu Zhengzong's poems praises him as a talent for bringing clarity—a sly compliment that defies all understanding.

sentences.zh: 正宗弟正學，為鄭成功總兵，正宗囑巡撫耿焞躐升中軍。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong's younger brother Zhengxue was a general under Zheng Chenggong; Liu Zhengzong directed Governor Geng Tun to leapfrog-promote him to Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong's younger brother Zhengxue had served as a general under Zheng Chenggong; Liu Zhengzong prevailed upon Governor Geng Tun to promote him out of turn to Central Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 蠹國亂政，其事非一端。

translations.literal: He undermines the state and disrupts governance—the instances are not limited to one.
translations.idiomatic: He has gnawed at the state and thrown governance into disorder—and the offenses do not stop at one.

sentences.zh: 請乾斷以杜禍萌」。

translations.literal: I request decisive judgment to nip the calamity in the bud.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the throne to act decisively and cut off this evil before it can sprout.

sentences.zh: 御史季振宜繼劾，亦及國祥、正學，並正宗貪賄營利諸事。

translations.literal: Censor Ji Zhenyi followed with impeachment, also touching on Guoxiang, Zhengxue, and Liu Zhengzong's matters of bribery and profiteering.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ji Zhenyi piled on with further impeachments, extending to Dong Guoxiang and Liu Zhengxue, and to Liu Zhengzong's bribery and self-enrichment as well.

sentences.zh: 正宗疏辨，略謂：「李昌祚為叛黨，裔介身為法司，何不早行糾參？

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong submitted a memorial in defense, briefly stating: Li Changzuo was a rebel party member—Wei Yijie himself is head of the judiciary, why did he not impeach early?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong answered with a defensive memorial, arguing in brief: Li Changzuo was a rebel—Wei Yijie himself heads the judiciary; why did he not move to impeach sooner?

sentences.zh: 例凡薦舉之官，在本任不職，追坐舉主。
