translations.literal: By precedent, for any official who was recommended, if he proves unfit in his current post, the recommender is held accountable.
translations.idiomatic: By established rule, when a recommended official fails in his new post, the fault is traced back to whoever recommended him.

sentences.zh: 國祥、羽明皆升任後得罪。

translations.literal: Guoxiang and Yuming both offended only after their promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming both fell only after they had already been promoted.

sentences.zh: 縉彥序臣詩有曰'將明之才'，臣詩稿見存，縉彥序未見此語。

translations.literal: It is alleged that Zhang Jinyan's preface to my poetry contains the words talent for bringing clarity; my poetry manuscript survives, yet Zhang Jinyan's preface contains no such phrase.
translations.idiomatic: They claim Zhang Jinyan's preface to my poems reads talent for bringing clarity—but my drafts still exist, and Zhang Jinyan's preface contains no such words.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上奪正宗官，下王大臣會鞫；

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor stripped Liu Zhengzong of office and ordered the princes and grand ministers to jointly interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor stripped Liu Zhengzong of rank and ordered the princes and senior ministers to try him jointly.

sentences.zh: 亦責裔介、振宜不早糾參，並奪官待質。

translations.literal: He also rebuked Wei Yijie and Ji Zhenyi for not impeaching earlier, and likewise stripped their offices pending examination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also rebuked Wei Yijie and Ji Zhenyi for failing to impeach sooner, and stripped them of office as well, pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 旋議上裔介、振宜劾正宗罪狀鞫實者十一事，罪當絞。

translations.literal: Soon the deliberation submitted the eleven impeachment charges against Liu Zhengzong by Wei Yijie and Ji Zhenyi that were verified through interrogation; the crime warranted strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the joint inquiry reported back: of the charges Wei Yijie and Ji Zhenyi had brought against Liu Zhengzong, eleven were substantiated—enough to warrant death by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 上斥「正宗性質暴戾，器量褊淺，持論偏私，處事執謬。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked: Liu Zhengzong's nature is violent and harsh, his capacity narrow and shallow, his arguments partisan, his handling of affairs stubbornly wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor denounced him: Liu Zhengzong is by nature violent and overbearing, small-minded and shallow, partisan in argument, and perverse in judgment.

sentences.zh: 惟事沽名好勝，罔顧大體，罪戾滋甚。

translations.literal: He only cares to purchase reputation and love victory, heedless of the larger good—his crimes grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: He cares only for reputation and winning arguments, with no regard for the larger interest—and his offenses have only deepened.

sentences.zh: 從寬免死，籍家產之半，入旗，不許回籍」。

translations.literal: Being lenient, death is remitted; half his family's property is confiscated; he is enrolled in the Banner system; he is not permitted to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Out of clemency his life is spared; half his family's property is confiscated; he is enrolled in the Banners; and he is forbidden to return home.

sentences.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，以世祖遺詔及正宗罪狀，當置重典，愍其衰老，貸之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Sacred Ancestor ascended; based on Shizu's testament and Liu Zhengzong's crimes, he should have received heavy punishment; pitying his advanced age, he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Kangxi Emperor took the throne; given the Shunzhi Emperor's dying testament and the record of Liu Zhengzong's crimes, he merited the severest penalty—but the new emperor, taking pity on his great age, granted him pardon.

sentences.zh: 未幾病卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 張縉彥，河南新鄭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jinyan was a native of Xinzheng, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinyan came from Xinzheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，自知縣行取授主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi under Chongzhen of Ming; selected from magistrate appointment to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination under the Chongzhen reign of Ming, rose from county magistrate by special selection to become a Director.

sentences.zh: 再授編修，擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Again appointed Compiler, promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made a Compiler, then promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，詣固山額真葉臣軍前納款，福王授以總督，乃遁去。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi year 1, he went to Gushan Ejen Echen's camp to surrender; the Prince of Fu appointed him governor, whereupon he fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he went to Gushan Ejen Echen's camp to submit; the Prince of Fu then appointed him governor—but he slipped away.

sentences.zh: 既，复受洪承疇招降。

translations.literal: Afterwards he again accepted Hong Chengchou's invitation to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accepted Hong Chengchou's summons and surrendered once more.

sentences.zh: 九年，以薦下吏部考核。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, through recommendation he entered Ministry of Personnel examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, on recommendation, he was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel for evaluation.

sentences.zh: 十年，授山東右布政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, appointed Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十七年，甄別三品以上大臣，降授江南徽寧道。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in the culling of ministers of third rank and above, demoted to Jiangnan Huaining Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when officials of third rank and above were sifted and reassigned, he was demoted to intendant of the Huaining Circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 裔介劾正宗，詞連縉彥，奪官逮訊。

translations.literal: When Wei Yijie impeached Liu Zhengzong, the charges implicated Zhang Jinyan; his office was stripped and he was arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yijie impeached Liu Zhengzong, the accusations dragged in Zhang Jinyan as well; Zhang was stripped of office and taken into custody for questioning.

sentences.zh: 御史蕭震疏劾縉彥編刻無聲戲，自稱「不死英雄」，惑人心，害風俗。

translations.literal: Censor Xiao Zhen memorialized impeaching Zhang Jinyan for compiling and publishing Silent Drama, calling himself the undying hero—misleading hearts and harming custom.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xiao Zhen memorialized against Zhang Jinyan for editing and printing Silent Drama, in which he styled himself the hero who cannot die—a work that misled minds and poisoned morals.

sentences.zh: 王大臣會鞫，論斬，上命貰死，籍其家，流徙寧古塔。

translations.literal: The princes and grand ministers jointly interrogated; sentenced to decapitation; the emperor ordered death remitted, confiscated his property, exiled to Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers tried him jointly and sentenced him to decapitation; the emperor commuted the death sentence, confiscated his estate, and sent him into exile at Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 尋死於戍所。

translations.literal: Soon he died in the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 論曰：剛林相太宗，與範文程、希福並命，祁充格掌記室，於創業宜皆有功。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Gang Lin served as chancellor under Hong Taiji, appointed together with Fan Wencheng and Hifu; Qi Chongge managed the secretariat—in founding the enterprise they should all have had merit.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Gang Lin served Hong Taiji as chancellor, appointed alongside Fan Wencheng and Hifu, while Qi Chongge kept the secretariat—each ought to have earned merit in the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 銓故明相，諳故事，與名夏皆善佔對。

translations.literal: Feng Quan was a former Ming chancellor, versed in precedent; he and Chen Mingxia were both skilled at responsive answers.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan, a former Ming chancellor, knew the old forms by heart; he and Chen Mingxia were both masters of quick, polished reply.

sentences.zh: 名夏勸進雖不用，以此邀峻擢。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia's counsel to advance the dynasty was not adopted, yet by this he sought steep promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia's advice on how the dynasty should move forward went unused, yet he parlayed even that into rapid advancement.

sentences.zh: 之遴、正宗各有所援引，知當時亦頗用事。

translations.literal: Chen Zhilin and Liu Zhengzong each had their own factions to draw on; one knows they were quite influential at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilin and Liu Zhengzong each commanded their own networks of patronage; at the time they plainly wielded considerable power.

sentences.zh: 際初運，都高位，而不足以堪之。

translations.literal: At the dawn of the new era they all held high positions, yet were not equal to bearing them.
translations.idiomatic: They rose to the highest offices at the dynasty's beginning, yet none proved equal to the burden.

sentences.zh: 誅夷削奪，曾莫之惜。

translations.literal: Execution, extermination, and stripping of rank—none was regretted.
translations.idiomatic: When they were executed, ruined, or stripped of rank, no one mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 正宗傾名夏，亦不免於罪，尤可鑑矣。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengzong toppled Chen Mingxia, yet could not escape guilt himself—especially worthy of taking as a lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengzong brought down Chen Mingxia, yet could not keep himself from falling—a warning if ever there was one.
